blocks.text: County Line Glen Valley, Langley: Neighbourhood Guide
Living in County Line Glen Valley, Langley

parts.t: Glen Valley is farm country on the south shore of the Fraser River in the northeast corner of Langley, toward the Abbotsford border. On MLS® it is part of the “County Line Glen Valley” sub-area. Near the river, flood questions join the usual rural ones.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 8, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the Township of Langley and the Agricultural Land Commission.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Homes for sale in County Line Glen Valley

parts.t: County Line Glen Valley offers a unique blend of scenic farmland, private acreages, and peaceful rural living in one of Langley’s most sought-after countryside communities. Known for its wide open spaces, quiet roads, and beautiful mountain and valley views, this area is ideal for buyers looking for privacy, room to grow, and a true country lifestyle while still being within driving distance to city amenities.

Explore spacious estate parcels, hobby farms, and distinctive country properties that provide opportunities for agriculture, equestrian use, or simply enjoying a more relaxed pace of life. Many homes in County Line Glen Valley feature large lots, detached shops, and long private driveways, making them perfect for those who value space, nature, and independence.

Despite its rural feel, the area offers convenient access to Langley, Abbotsford, and major commuter routes, allowing residents to enjoy the best of both worlds — quiet acreage living with nearby shopping, schools, and services just a short drive away.

blocks.text: Flood, ALR and planning in County Line Glen Valley

parts.t: On farmland beside a big river, the rules and the water decide what a property is really worth to you.
The Rural Plan says floodplain development must conform to floodplain protection policies and regulations.
The Township runs regular dike inspections and a Freshet Flood Response Plan tied to water levels at the Mission Gauge.
The Glen Valley and Salmon River Flood Mitigation project, led by the Township with Kwantlen First Nation and the Rivershed Society of BC, covers dike bank repairs, culverts and added pump capacity.
The Rural Plan says most of the land in the rural area is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. ALR status is set property by property, so check the exact address.
About 75% of the Township’s land is in the ALR.
Streamside setbacks are measured from the top of bank or edge of floodplain, for example 30 m for a Class A watercourse.
Groundwater supplies about 80% of the Township’s water needs, and residents off the municipal system rely on at least 5,000 private wells.

What is in Glen Valley Regional Park?
River access along the Fraser, with the main entrance at
via 272 Street. Activities include fishing with a tidal waters licence, canoeing and kayaking, and dogs are allowed on leash.
On SD35’s catchment maps, Glen Valley falls in the Fort Langley Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary catchments. The maps are dated 2014, so check the exact address with the
Where does the name Glen Valley come from?
Glen Valley is an official BC geographic name. The area was earlier called Beaver Valley and Cromarty’s Prairie, and the Glen Valley Post Office ran from 1904 to 1968.
The Province gave $5 million to the Glen Valley and Salmon River Flood Mitigation project. The provincial dike inventory includes the Glen Valley Dyking District.
